title: docker.GetDigest fails when HOME is unset and the uid has no passwd entry (regression from containers/image v5.36.2)
body:
With go.podman.io/image/v5 v5.42.0 (go.podman.io/storage v1.65.0), every registry
lookup fails when HOME is unset and the current uid has no `/etc/passwd` entry:
```
    unable to resolve HOME directory: user: unknown userid 4321
```
github.com/containers/image/v5 v5.36.2 succeeds in the same environment.

To reproduce (CGO_ENABLED=0 build), as a uid without a passwd entry and an empty environment:
```
    setpriv --reuid=4321 --regid=4321 --clear-groups env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin ./lookup
```
where ./lookup calls docker.ParseReference + docker.GetDigest against any registry,
with SystemContext{DockerAuthConfig: &types.DockerAuthConfig{}} (no credential discovery).

**Potential root cause**: `dockerCertDir` now calls `configfile.GetSearchPaths`, whose `UserConfigPath` returns the error from `unshare.HomeDir()`. v5.36.2 used `homedir.Get()`, which returned "" and
carried on. The user cert directory is optional, so an unresolvable home could skip
it rather than fail the whole client.

**Also related**: UserConfigPath uses os.LookupEnv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME"), so a set-but-empty
XDG_CONFIG_HOME yields the relative path "containers/certs.d".

comments.body:
\*shrug\* don’t do that? Among other things, POSIX explicitly requires `HOME` to be set, and that implies that a home directory must actually be a defined concept.

Also, running under an unallocated UID looks, if anything, like an attack. I don’t know why such a setup should be worth even discussing.
I could see some CI environments mission some of that and something that came up when trying to migrate from old docker module.
